basics.name: Karthik Kannan
basics.label: Mechanical & Aerospace Engineer
basics.summary: Mechanical and Aerospace Engineer with a multidisciplinary background spanning aerospace structures, AI/ML, autonomy, and systems integration. Experienced in leading UAV projects, writing autonomy algorithms, and working with NASA, FEMA, and Collier Aerospace. Motivated to push innovation in aerospace and robotics.

work.name: Collier Aerospace – Sponsored by NASA NC Space Grant
work.summary: Worked on structural analysis, automation, and research funded through NASA NC Space Grant.
highlights: Analyzed and sized composite and metallic aerospace structures using HyperX, optimizing strength-to-weight ratios.
Performed FEA in FEMAP and NASTRAN to assess stresses, load paths, and margins of safety.
Conducted material and architectural trade studies, producing documentation for NASA, Blue Origin, Electra and Boeing.
Spearheaded a new conductive documentation pipeline, unifying HyperX output with Excel reporting.
Worked on several proprietary internal projects, and created unique scripting stress reports
Bridged engineering and software by building Python-based automation tools for HyperX workflows.
Presented automation methods at a NASA symposium showcasing aerospace software innovation.
Researched spar optimization and wing box architecture to improve efficiency and manufacturability.

work.name: REACHR Project – NC State University
work.summary: Led autonomy, controls, and structures development for FEMA-backed HERO 2 amphibious UAV.
highlights: Designed and implemented autonomous flight control algorithms for stability and navigation.
Integrated avionics including GPS, IMUs, barometers, and telemetry for real-time health monitoring.
Built hardware-in-the-loop simulations and test plans for autonomous validation.
Coordinated interdisciplinary teams across AI/ML, avionics, and mechanical systems.
Demonstrated field testing at Ocracoke Island for FEMA disaster-response operations.
Developed computer vision modules for autonomous landing and obstacle avoidance.

work.name: GoAero Prize – RESCURE PACK Team
work.summary: Represented NC State in a national UAV competition, winning Phase 1 and securing $30,000 in funding.
highlights: Led structural design and AI/ML integration for RPAC (Rescue Pack) UAV.
Built object detection and terrain classification systems for disaster-response autonomy.
Derived aircraft equations of motion to support advanced flight control design.
Managed integration across structures, avionics, and AI subsystems.
Served as team spokesperson on WRAL news and FEMA-aligned presentations.
Authored technical reports, FEMA use cases, and funding proposals.

work.name: Teaching Assistant – NC State University
work.summary: Supported aerospace courses including Intro to Aerospace, Structures, and Applied Aerodynamics.
highlights: Assisted over 150 students through labs, grading, and structured review sessions.
Led demos on aerodynamic flow visualization and structural testing.
Collaborated with professors on curriculum design and assessments.
Maintained a high-energy teaching style recognized by students and faculty.

work.name: Four Colors Tech
work.summary: Worked at early-stage AI startup on proprietary LLM-powered enterprise assistant (COG).
highlights: Optimized large language models for PLM and CAD data environments.
Fine-tuned NLP models for classification, summarization, and revision tracking.
Built self-healing automation systems for enterprise workflows.
Streamlined automation pipelines with Playwright and Selenium, cutting QA time by 40%.
Secured training datasets using masking and anonymization strategies.
Supported NX CAD optimization workflows and PLM standardization strategies.

work.name: Undead Electronics
work.summary: Repaired and serviced electronics in a fast-paced repair environment.
highlights: Diagnosed and repaired 100+ devices including phones, laptops, and tablets.
Performed micro-soldering and IC replacement for motherboard repair.
Recovered and migrated customer data from damaged devices.
Maintained repair documentation and improved shop intake workflows.

work.name: Zaloni
work.summary: Developed automation solutions for healthcare data pipelines at enterprise data company.
highlights: Built automated pipelines to catalog DICOM medical images and records.
Developed parsers in Java/Python to integrate metadata into SQL Server.
Deployed a production system at Duke Hospitals saving $100,000 annually.
Improved fault tolerance and batch-processing speed for clinical data ingestion.

education.summary: Focus in aerospace structures, AI/ML in engineering.
Graduated Magna Cum Laude. Dean’s List every semester.
Minor in Computer Science complementing engineering degree.
